{"base":"main","body":"Closes #58\r\n\r\n## What changed and why\r\n\r\nGitHub users move around a repository with two-key `g` shortcuts, and Gitea had none. Building on #56's registry, this PR adds them: `g c`, `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` go to a repository's Code, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions and Wiki tabs, and `g n` goes to the user's notifications from any page.\r\n\r\n- **A link can declare its own shortcut.** A link in a template that carries a few attributes registers a shortcut that goes where the link leads. The shortcut only exists while the link is on the page, so it follows whatever the template already decides about the link.\r\n- **The tab bar declares the repository shortcuts.** Each tab marks itself, so a tab that isn't shown (its feature is turned off, the user can't read it, or it is Actions on an empty repository) has no shortcut. The external issue tracker and external wiki tabs aren't marked, so a shortcut never leaves Gitea. Tabs that move into the \"more\" menu on a narrow window are still on the page, so their shortcuts keep working.\r\n- **`g c` goes to the repository's front page,** not where the Code tab links: on a branch other than the default, the Code tab points at that branch.\r\n- **`g n` is declared on the notifications bell,** which only signed-in users have. The bell is in the page twice, once for phones and once for desktops, so only one copy declares it.\r\n- **Each shortcut is listed with its tab's translated name** (\"Issues\", without the open count), in the \"Repository\" section with `s` and `t`. `g n` is \"Notifications\" under a new \"General\" string, which #57's help dialog will also use for `?`.\r\n- The docs in `.claude-students` are updated with the new way to add a shortcut.\r\n\r\n## How the changes relate to the ACs\r\n\r\n- **AC1:** `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` on a repository page go to that tab.\r\n- **AC2:** `g c` goes to the repository's front page on the default branch, even while browsing another branch.\r\n- **AC3:** a tab that is not shown declares no shortcut, so its keys do nothing.\r\n- **AC4:** the external tracker and wiki tabs declare no shortcut, so `g i` and `g w` do nothing there and the browser stays in Gitea.\r\n- **AC5:** tabs in the \"more\" menu are still on the page, so their shortcuts work.\r\n- **AC6:** signed in, `g n` goes to notifications from any page; signed out there is no bell, so it does nothing.\r\n- **AC7:** outside a repository there is no tab bar, so the repository shortcuts do nothing.\r\n- **AC8:** each repository shortcut has its tab's name in the Repository section, and `g n` is \"Notifications\" under \"General\".\r\n\r\n## How it was tested\r\n\r\n### Test strategy\r\n\r\nMost of the risk in this PR is in the wiring, not the code: whether a shortcut exists is decided by the templates, so most mistakes only show up on a real page. The tests are split along that line.\r\n\r\n- **Unit tests (Vitest) for the part that is plain code.** Turning a link into a shortcut needs no server, so it is tested on its own, where the tests are fast and a failure points straight at the cause. The 4 new tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` target the three places where the obvious version would be wrong: a description taken from the link's text would include the open count, following the link would keep `g c` on the browsed branch, and treating a hidden link as gone would break the \"more\" menu. They are named `#58 AC…`, because the other tests in that file use #56's AC numbers.\r\n- **Playwright tests for the wiring.** A unit test can't see which tabs a template renders. Each of the 4 new tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` sets up the one situation where a wiring mistake would show: a branch other than the default, the only time `g c` and the Code tab disagree; turned-off and external tabs, the only time a shortcut could outlive its tab or leave Gitea; a narrow window, the only time tabs move; and a signed-in user, the only time there are two bells to clash. On an ordinary page each of these mistakes would pass unnoticed. A new `apiEditRepo` helper in `tests/e2e/utils.ts` sets up the repository with the turned-off and external tabs.\r\n- **Proving that nothing happened.** A test that presses a dead shortcut and sees nothing would also pass on a page where no key works at all. The AC3 and AC4 test therefore presses a live shortcut (`s`) after the dead ones and checks that it still runs.\r\n\r\n**Testing the tests.** Each test was checked via mutation testing to ensure that the tests actually detect something real. For the unit tests: taking the description from the link's text, dropping the section, an action that does nothing, ignoring a link's own address, and treating a hidden part of the page as gone. For the Playwright tests: the Code tab without its own address, a shortcut on the external tracker tab, both bells declaring `g n`, and treating hidden elements as gone. Each break failed the matching tests, and #56's tests stayed green.\r\n\r\n**Not covered automatically, and why.** AC3's other cases, a tab the user can't read and Actions on an empty repository, aren't driven separately. The template hides those tabs the same way it hides a turned-off one, which the AC3 test covers.\r\n\r\n**Checked by hand.** Claude also drove a headless browser through a local instance: the tab shortcuts, `g c` from a branch, a narrow window, and `g n` signed in and out. I spot checked the shortcuts myself as well, checking that the new commands actually work and shift focus to the correct sections on the page ( `g c`, `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` go to the Code, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions and Wiki tabs respectively). Of course, I also ran the lint suite as provided by gitea and ran the appropriate tests to ensure they actually function (vitest unit tests, playwright for e2e, and checking that a clash does not happen).\r\n\r\n| AC | What the tests check |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| AC1 | `g i`, `g p`, `g a` and `g w` each go to their tab on a real repository; a link's shortcut goes where the link leads |\r\n| AC2 | On a branch other than the default, the Code tab links to that branch and `g c` goes to the front page; a link's shortcut can go to its own address |\r\n| AC3 | With pull requests and Actions turned off, no `g p` or `g a` is declared, the keys do nothing and a live shortcut still runs after them |\r\n| AC4 | With an external tracker and wiki, their tabs are shown but declare nothing, the keys do nothing and no new tab opens |\r\n| AC5 | At 420 px wide the Wiki tab is in the \"more\" menu and `g w` still works; a link moved into a hidden part of the page keeps its shortcut |\r\n| AC6 | Signed out there is no `g n`; signed in there is exactly one, and it goes to notifications |\r\n| AC7 | On `/explore/repos` no repository shortcut is declared |\r\n| AC8 | Issues is \"Issues\" in \"Repository\", and `g n` is \"Notifications\" in \"General\"; a link is listed with its own description, not its text |\r\n\r\n## CI / manual verification\r\n\r\n- CI runs on the PR; per the course rules, it must pass before merging.\r\n- `make test-frontend`: 361 tests pass, including the 4 new ones.\r\n- `make lint-js`, `make lint-templates`, `make lint-editorconfig` and the locale JSON lint pass.\r\n- The 7 Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` pass locally on Chromium and Firefox; each new one runs in under 1.5 s.\r\n- `./.claude-students/check.sh` reports only the two `models-issues.md` size limits, which were failing before this PR.\r\n\r\n## Design\r\n\r\nDesign decisions noted under issue #58.\r\n\r\n## Tech Debt\r\n\r\n**Introduced:**\r\n- `g n` and the tabs in the \"more\" menu rely on #56 counting a hidden element as present. The bell that declares `g n` is the phone-layout copy, which is hidden on desktops, and tabs in the closed \"more\" menu are hidden too. If the registry ever started ignoring hidden elements, as #56's Tech Debt suggests later shortcuts might need, both would stop working. The Playwright tests for AC5 and AC6 fail if that happens.\r\n\r\n**Encountered:**\r\n- The navbar renders its icons, the notifications bell among them, twice: once for the phone layout and once for desktop, with CSS hiding one. For a signed-in user both copies are in the page, unless they must change their password first, so marking both with `g n` makes #56's registry throw a clash on every page. Handled by a `WithShortcut` flag that only the copy rendered for every signed-in user passes. The core issue of two notification bells was not fixed here.\r\n\r\n## Implementation Note\r\nDespite the changes impacting the user-facing experience, there are no UI changes that require before and after screenshots. As confusing as this may be, these shortcuts only take the user to another page, and don't add, remove or change any element on the page.\r\n\r\n## AI assistance\r\n\r\nClaude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes, and ran the headless-browser checks and the checks that each test fails when its code is broken. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I could review each one with its tests. +// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
+export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
+  registerShortcut({
+    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
+    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
+    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
+    element: link,
+    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
+  });
+}

Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab never reaches the page behind it. The user presses Escape. The dialog closes, and focus returns to where it was.
13:- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the element that had focus before the dialog opened.
15:- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, a textarea or an editable area, when the user types `?`, then a `?` character appears in the field and the dialog does not open.
16:- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut that later code registers with a new section appears under that section, with no change to the dialog's code.
17:- [ ] AC6: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the title, the close button's accessible name and the "General" heading come from locale keys.

43:**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and that new features must not use it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal in an accessibility feature works against #25. `showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert (AC3), closes the dialog on Escape (AC2) and sets `aria-modal`. Option (b) would rewrite behaviour that the browser already has, and hand-written focus handling causes the kind of bug that #25 fixes.
45:**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.
48:**Decision:** Render the empty `<dialog>` once in the base page template, next to the footer script, and keep it hidden until it opens. The server renders the translated title, close label and "General" heading. When the user presses `?`, JavaScript adds the rows from `getShortcuts()`.
54:**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.
56:**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `s` and `t` shortcuts register from a `<kbd>` hint on the page, but `?` has no hint. JavaScript registers `?` instead, and reads its description and "General" label from data attributes on the dialog.

- **Two-key shortcuts.** Rows like `g c` hold two keys, so the dialog has to show one `<kbd>` per key. Your spec only shows single keys (`?`, `S`, `T`), so that case needs handling.
